15C.1 We should be of aid and help to the fatherless and widows with their afflictions.

precepts.text: For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light. That is the light Job walked by.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
Job looks back on his life: “Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me; When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness”. When his candle shined upon my head: the Holy Spirit was on me. But what does “by his light I walked through darkness” mean?

“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The commandment is the lamp, and the law is the light.

That is the light Job walked by. We can only walk through darkness the way Job did: with God’s commandments. Job kept the law, and that law was the light that carried him through a dark world.

precepts.text: The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law. That is the secret of God upon Job's tabernacle, and the relationship between Job and us.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
“As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle”. What is the secret of God? This shows the relationship between Job and us.

“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

God reveals his secrets to the Israelites. The things revealed belong to us and to our children for ever, and they are revealed for a purpose: that we may do all the words of this law. The secret of God was upon Job’s tabernacle because he was of that people, and he kept that law.

precepts.text: Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, and they shall judge the people with just judgment. Job prepared his seat in the street: he was one of these judges.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
“When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street!” What does that mean, he prepared his seat in the street?

“Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.”

So Job was a judge. He sat in the gate and judged the people with just judgment. That is why “The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up. The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.” When Job rolled on the scene, everybody shut the hell up. Princes covered their mouths, young men moved the hell out of the way, and the old men stood up and saluted him. The nobles held their peace; they had nothing to say either. That is total respect and honor.

precepts.text: He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow. Delivering the fatherless and the poor goes into God's law.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
“Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.” Job is telling you what he used to do. The fatherless are the orphans, and he delivered them and the ones who had no one to help.

That goes into God’s law: “He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.”

Job judged the way God judges. And he did not stop there: “The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.” When somebody is about to die and wants to speak to you, sometimes you are at a loss for words and do not know what to say to bring them comfort. Job knew exactly what to say. Then he comforted the widow, mourning and crying because her husband just died.

That is a hard thing. You have to pray to the Lord: give me the words. You have to let a dying believer know, it is going to be okay; even when you leave this world, you are going to be all right. When we die, that is not the end of it for us, and that is what comforts us.

precepts.text: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
“I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.” Whatever Job did not know, he searched out. Sometimes brothers try to fake stuff. Don’t fake it. Job said, if I did not know it, I searched it out.

Christ said it: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.”

We have to get to that point. Search it out. Get the Who’s Who with the Apocrypha, get your Zondervan Bible dictionary, get the complete works of Josephus, get your concordance, and do your own work. Before you ask us a question, how about you search it out, and then ask your question after you have done research on it. That is what Job did with every cause he did not know.

precepts.text: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. That was the attribute Job had, and we have to be the same way.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
“These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”

That was the attribute Job had: “the cause which I knew not I searched out.” The Bereans received the word with all readiness of mind, and they searched the scriptures daily to see whether the things they were taught were so. That made them more noble.

We have to be the same way. Search things out daily. Do not just hear it and move on, and do not come asking without having looked first. A father to the poor, a judge in the gate, and a man who searched out what he did not know: that is the kind of man Job was, and the kind we have to become.

precepts.text: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God. That is what Job was doing when men gave ear and waited at his counsel.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
“My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand. Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.” Job was up there. He was no pushover, no punk.

This is what Jethro told Moses: “Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God”.

That is what Job was doing. He was for the people to God-ward, bringing their causes to God, and men waited in silence for his counsel. “After my words they spake not again”: after Job spoke, you had nothing to say. “I chose out their way, and sat chief”: he counseled them and directed them, and dwelt as a king in the army.

precepts.text: My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew. When Job spoke it was like that; and that right there is prophetic, it is going to come again in the future.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
“And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.” They waited for his words with their mouths open. When he was teaching or giving counsel, he was dropping blessings on them, dropping understanding.

It says the same thing as the song of Moses: “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass”.

So when Job spoke, it was like that: “my speech dropped upon them.” And that right there is prophetic. It is going to come again in the future, near to come.

precepts.text: Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy. Job put on righteousness and it clothed him.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.
precepts.why:
“I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.” That shows you how Job used to dress. The way he dressed, that is how his righteousness reflected.

“Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.”

That is why it was written down beside Job 29:14. Sometimes you just scribble in your Bible, and when you look at it again you see why. God wants his priests clothed with righteousness, and Job put on righteousness and it clothed him. His outward robe and diadem matched the righteousness he walked in, and the saints shout for joy when the righteous are clothed that way.

points: Who exactly was Job? In this chapter Job is reflecting on his life. Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me: when my life was good, my kids were with me, my businesses were flourishing.
When his candle shined upon my head: the Holy Spirit was on me. And when by his light I walked through darkness: we can only walk through darkness, like Job did, with God's commandments.
When the secret of God was upon my tabernacle: God reveals his secrets to the Israelites.
When I washed my steps with butter: a smooth life. And the rock poured me out rivers of oil.

When I prepared my seat in the street: Job was a judge. The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up. The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth. When Job rolled on the scene, princes covered their mouths, young men moved out of the way, and the old men stood up and saluted him. The nobles held their peace.
When the ear heard me, then it blessed me: total respect and honor. Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.

The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow's heart to sing for joy. When somebody is about to die and wants to speak to you, sometimes you are at a loss for words. Job was the type of man who knew exactly what to say, and then he comforted the widow in her mourning. You have to pray to the Lord: give me the words, because it is a hard thing. Even in death, a believer can be told: it is going to be okay; even when you leave this world, you are going to be all right.
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem. The way Job dressed, his righteousness reflected it.

I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame. I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out. Whatever Job did not know, he did not fake: he searched it out. We have to get to that point. Get your study tools: the who's who with the Apocrypha, your Bible dictionary, your Complete Works of Josephus, your concordance. Before you ask a question, search it out, then ask after you have done research.
And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth: whatever the wicked stole, Job took it back. That is forefather Job right there. He was not a pushover.

Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel. After my words they spake not again: after Job spoke, you had nothing to say. And my speech dropped upon them, and they waited for me as for the rain, and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain: he was dropping blessings and understanding on them.

If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.

When Job went out to the gate, the place where the leaders sat to judge matters, the young men saw him and hid themselves, and the aged arose and stood up. As Job made his entry, as leaders make their entry, it is a law to rise up before them. They thought we made that up, bishop on deck, IUIC doing their own thing; no, we are following the commandments of God.
Remember verse 1 says Job continued his parable. A lot of what Job is talking about, not the entire book but a lot of it, is in parable form, and most of it is above the pay grade.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: Job continues his parable and remembers the months past when the Most High preserved him, when His candle shined upon his head and by His light Job walked through darkness.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: These were the days of his youth, when the secret of God was upon his tabernacle, when the Almighty was yet with him and his children were about him, when he washed his steps with butter and the rock poured him out rivers of oil.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: When Job went out to the gate of the city and prepared his seat in the street, the young men saw him and hid themselves, and the aged arose and stood up.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: The princes refrained talking and laid their hand on their mouth. The nobles held their peace and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth. When the ear heard him it blessed him, and when the eye saw him it gave witness to him.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: Job delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him. The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon him, and he caused the widow's heart to sing for joy.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: He put on righteousness and it clothed him, his judgment was as a robe and a diadem. He was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame, a father to the poor, and he searched out the cause he knew not. He broke the jaws of the wicked and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: Then Job said he would die in his nest and multiply his days as the sand. His root was spread out by the waters and the dew lay all night upon his branch. His glory was fresh in him and his bow was renewed in his hand.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: Men gave ear to Job and waited and kept silence at his counsel. After his words they spake not again, and his speech dropped upon them. They waited for him as for the rain and opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.

note.label: Job 29: The Days When The Most High Preserved Me

points: If he laughed on them they believed it not, and the light of his countenance they cast not down. He chose out their way and sat chief, dwelling as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. This is a deep parable by Job.
